### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you!
  
  
Under the close supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) and Cannabis Program Manager, the Environmental Scientist performs professional scientific analyses and fieldwork associated with appropriate use of pesticides and supports DPR’s Cannabis Program. Applies scientific methods and principles to perform environmental investigations, analyses, research and studies for compliance with toxic and hazardous pesticide restrictions. Provides oversight of enforcement compliance to maintain statewide uniformity. Incumbent generates, analyzes and evaluates scientific data for regulatory compliance with human health and environmental requirements, providing protections from pesticide use on human health, non-target vegetation, cannabis cultivation, food safety, surface/ground water, wildlife, and air quality.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

The incumbent works in a single-floor building under artificial lighting. The collection of samples as indicated for this position requires the ability to lift and carry a minimum of 40 pounds, bend, squat, and climb over boxes, containers, or pallets; travel by automobile or air may be required to different areas of the State. There is field work performed requiring the ability to maneuver over uneven ground and work in outdoor conditions. Occasional statewide travel may be required. Occasional irregular work schedules may be required. Travel may include overnight stays several days each month.
  
  
**NOTE:** This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.
  
  
Beginning July 1, 2026, it is anticipated the position will be office-centered and employees will be expected to report to the office at least four days per week.

Our core values include accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and integrity. We are innovative and passionate about the work we do.
  
  
DPR values diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout the organization. We foster an environment where employees from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. We believe the diversity of our employees is essential to inspiring innovative solutions. Together we further our mission to protect human health and the environment by fostering sustainable pest management and regulating pesticides. Join DPR to improve the lives of all Californians.

jobs.title: Deputy Chief Environmental Scientist, Science and Public Health Partnerships
jobs.description:
**Overview**
------------

**Work Type:** Ongoing - Full-time

**Salary:** $193,946 - $263,771

**Grade:** VPS 7

**Occupation:** Science and research

**Location:** Melbourne - Northern suburbs

**Reference:** 1831

**Role details:** Ongoing, full time | VPS 7 | $193,946 to $263,771 + 12% superannuation | Centre for Applied Sciences, Ernest Jones Drive, Macleod VIC 3085

  

* **Shape Victoria’s environmental science and public health strategy**
* **Build high-value research, government and industry partnerships**
* **Translate leading science and research into regulatory innovation**
  

**About the organisation**

Environment Protection Authority Victoria (EPA) is Victoria’s environmental regulator, working to prevent and reduce the harmful effects of pollution and waste on Victorians and their environment. EPA is a values and purpose-driven organisation that works with community, government and industry to deliver for all Victorians. As an independent statutory authority, EPA uses its powers and tools to prevent risks to the environment and human health.

  

**About the role**

As Deputy Chief Environmental Scientist, Science and Public Health Strategy and Partnerships, you will lead EPA’s Science Strategy, Partnerships and Public Health branch, driving sustainable operations and partnerships, technical leadership of science research and development strategy, regulatory innovation and environmental public health influence. Reporting to the Chief Environmental Scientist, you will provide senior executive support and strategic advice on complex science, public health and partnership matters, and represent EPA externally when required. You will provide executive sponsorship for EPA’s Centre of Excellence for Regulatory Science and Innovation model, build high-value partnerships across universities, research institutes, government, industry and health agencies, and lead the development of EPA’s science, digital innovation and environmental public health strategies. Taking a One Health lens, you will integrate science, engineering and research capabilities to strengthen environmental and public health outcomes.

  

**About you**

You are an established scientific and environmental public health leader with extensive experience integrating multidisciplinary health, environmental science and engineering disciplines to translate evidence into strategy and action. You have demonstrated senior executive leadership experience in a complex scientific, public health or regulatory environment and the capability to act as a trusted deputy to a chief scientist or equivalent executive. You bring experience developing strategy, establishing priorities, managing risk and translating strategic direction into practical delivery, together with experience in major research programs, centres of excellence or strategic partnership models. You can influence senior stakeholders, negotiate complex outcomes and clearly communicate scientific, environmental public health and strategic issues to executive, governing board, government, partners and public audiences. A doctorate or relevant postgraduate qualification in environmental public health or a related discipline is required.

  

**How to apply**

Click **‘Apply’** to submit your application, including a cover letter addressing your experience, the key selection criteria, motivations and suitability for the role, and a resume including contact details for two referees.

**Department for Environment and Water**
  
**Job reference:** 862707
  
**Location:** 5000 - ADELAIDE
  
**Job status:** Long Term Contract
  
**Eligibility:** Open to Everyone

**Make a Difference Through Environmental Data**

Put your data design and modelling expertise to work protecting South Australia’s environment.

In this role, you’ll design and maintain data models that help make complex environmental information accessible, reliable and useful. Working with scientists, technical specialists and policy teams, you’ll support better data management and informed decision-making across the department.

An exciting challenge will be working with complex biodiversity datasets in an advanced knowledge graph environment.

With an initial focus on supporting the Biodiversity Act 2025 and delivering BioData SA, you’ll help build the data foundations needed to support biodiversity protection and environmental management across South Australia.

**Bring your expertise. Build better data. Make a difference.**

  

**What can we offer you!**

* Working in an organisation that is contributing to significant environmental outcomes in the great state of South Australia!
* Be part of a fun, collaborative and supportive team.
* Hybrid working model with flexible working options including work from home available to promote work life balance.
* Free entry into DEW managed Parks in South Australia.
* Salary Sacrifice Benefits.
* Access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
* Access to our Fitness Passport Program.
* Meaningful and rewarding career.

2 year contract

* May be required to participate in responses to state emergencies or associated duties.

* This role requires candidates to provide a Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check which must be renewed every three years before expiry. DEW will cover the cost of renewal.
* May be required to undertake intra or interstate travel, occasional overnight absences, and work outside of the normal hours of work.

A successful applicant who is not currently employed by the Department for Environment and Water will be required to have an original photo identification document sighted and provide a valid Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check (NCCHC) issued within the last 12 months. This information must be supplied by all applicants who are shortlisted for interview.

jobs.title: Principal Consultant / Technical Director - Ecotoxicology & Ecological Risk Assessment
jobs.description:
**Principal Consultant / Technical Director – Ecotoxicology & Ecological Risk Assessment**

  

Lead Technical Excellence. Shape Strategy. Grow a Market-Leading Practice.

Are you an established **Ecotoxicologist or Ecological Risk Assessor** looking for an opportunity to build your profile, influence major projects, and help shape the future direction of a growing environmental consultancy practice?

  

We are seeking an experienced **Principal Consultant or Technical Director** to join and lead our **Ecotoxicology and Ecological Risk Assessment group as part of the Toxicology & Risk team** . This is a key technical and business role for a recognised industry professional with a strong technical reputation, established client relationships, and a passion for growing business and developing people.

  

As a key member within our **Soils, Geochemistry, Toxicology and Risk Practice** , you will work alongside a highly regarded team of specialist consultants, including a dedicated ecotoxicology group and a broader multidisciplinary practice of more than 40+ experts across Asia Pacific.

  

This is more than a technical leadership role. It is an opportunity to join a collaborative team that combines deep technical expertise with a strong growth mindset. You will have the autonomy to shape the direction of the ecotoxicology practice while being supported by a substantial multidisciplinary network of specialists who are solving some of the most complex environmental challenges across the region.

  

We have just over 1,200 staff in Asia Pacific and you will find us located in all the major cities and many regional areas. We are open to location for the successful person where we have established offices in place.

  

**Responsibilities**

Working with other technical specialists who are passionate about their fields and highly collaborative employees, this role offers the platform to:

  

* Lead and grow a successful ecotoxicology and ecological risk assessment capability.
* Drive business development and work-winning initiatives across existing and emerging markets.
* Leverage your professional network and industry profile to identify opportunities and develop long-term client partnerships.
* Provide technical leadership on complex environmental, contaminated land, mining, industrial, infrastructure and regulatory projects.
* Mentor and develop a team of talented ecotoxicologists and risk assessment specialists.
* Collaborate with leading experts across contaminated land, geochemistry, toxicology, human health risk assessment, hydrogeology and environmental sciences.
Influence strategic direction, service offerings and market growth within a well-established environmental consulting business.  

  

**Experience**

Not only will you be a honest, trusted and great person to be around, you will also be a recognised technical leader who brings:

  

* Relevant tertiary qualifications in ecotoxicology, environmental science, ecology, toxicology or a related discipline coupled with 10-15+ years’ experience ( *ideally within a consulting environment but open to other industry)*
* A strong reputation within industry, regulatory, government and/or commercial sectors.
* Demonstrated success in winning work, developing client relationships and generating revenue growth.
* Established networks and connections that can contribute to the continued expansion of the practice.
* Experience leading multidisciplinary project teams and mentoring technical professionals.
* Strong commercial acumen and the ability to identify and capitalise on market opportunities.
Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.  

  

**Our Benefits**

We are most proud of our expert teams and unique culture where we work together to collaborate on projects to get the best possible outcome for our clients.

  

Whether you’re enjoying our flexible hybrid work environment, taking advantage of our novated leasing offers, or at a time in your life where a supportive and generous parental leave scheme is key, our benefits aim to ensure that we cater for all.

  

You can find a comprehensive list **here.**

  

**Next Steps**

If leading an established and premier team at a global multidisciplinary consultancy is your next career move, apply now with a copy of your CV and cover letter.

  

*Unsolicited resumes from recruitment consultants will not be accepted. You must be part of the preferred supplier agreement list which is coordinated through our Talent Acquisition team.*
